From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Rivera <dana.rivera@greenleaf.health>, Paul Chen <paul.chen@greenleaf.health>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: MAP execution: initial results (raw summaries attached)

Team — completed the controlled runs. High-level summary (attached CSV contains full traces):

- Latency (p50 / p95) for 50-token profile (fp16 model):
  - US-West: 12 ms / 48 ms
  - EU-Central: 28 ms / 96 ms
  - APAC-SG: 72 ms / 210 ms

- TTFT (50-token) cold vs warmed (median):
  - Cold (first 100 requests after 30m idle): US-West 42 ms, EU-Central 85 ms, APAC-SG 160 ms
  - Warmed: US-West 11 ms, EU-Central 26 ms, APAC-SG 68 ms

- Throughput and concurrency (1024-token stress profile, fp16):
  - Single-region sustained throughput @ 200 concurrent connections (tokens/s): US-West 15.6k t/s, EU-Central 11.2k t/s, APAC-SG 7.1k t/s
  - Ramp to 2k concurrent (mixed-size traffic): observed tail latency degradation past ~1.2k concurrent in EU and APAC. US-West maintained p95 < 300ms up to 1.8k.

- Failover / routing switch tests (drain us-west):
  - Latency-first routing: median cutover 18s, transient error spike (5xx) for ~6s during inflight reroutes.
  - Strict-region policy (reject when region unavailable): cutover led to 100% request failure until manual re-route (~42s).
  - Cost-fallback routing: cutover 24s, slightly higher downstream latency but fewer errors vs latency-first in sustained traffic.

- Resource notes: GPU utilization at peak ~92% in US-West tests; EU and APAC showed GPU queuing where tail latencies rose.

I'm attaching raw CSV and region traces. Next steps: Vivek will run a tuned routing policy and provide cost delta numbers for each policy.

-Stephanie

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: MAP deliverable: routing policy recommendation & cost delta estimates

Team — attached is the recommendation. TL;DR: for Greenleaf's SLA (p95 < 150ms for 50-token flows, < 500ms for 1024-token flows) we recommend a hybrid routing policy "latency-primary with graceful-cost-fallback". Key findings:

- Performance fit: latency-primary keeps p95 well within SLA in US and EU for small responses; APAC will need either regional capacity increase or preferential warm-cache pinning to meet p95 for 50-token flows.
- Failover behavior: hybrid policy achieves median cutover 20–25s with a short error spike (~4–7s). Strict-region is unacceptable for user-facing traffic.
- Cost delta: switching from strict-region to latency-primary increases estimated monthly egress/compute by ~14% for mixed traffic; cost-fallback adds ~6% more under storm scenarios. Detailed per-route numbers in the CSV attached.

Proposed close timeline within the MAP:
- July 7: finalize routing policy and produce Canary config for Greenleaf staging.
- July 9–10: 48-hour canary with live production traffic at 10% (observe SLOs).
- July 12: full rollout & billing change notice.

Call to action: Dana/Paul — please confirm you want us to proceed with the hybrid config and the 10% canary window. We'll prepare the Canary runbook and DocuSign amendment for committed capacity if you accept the cost delta.

-Vivek
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
